purpose: Teach: フレッツ/エンタテイメント/ラストシーン/ポッドキャスティング/ヤンキース/ソフトボール/ホステス/タッグ
target_vocab: ポッドキャスティング

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがフレッツ光の初期契約をされた
lines.en: Gran, your father used to watch Flets streaming when he was younger.
lines.style: Soft, remembering tone. Eyes slightly distant. Gentle lift on 'your father' — not accusatory, just calling up an old image. Pause before speaking, as if retrieving from deep memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、エンタテイメント番組をお楽しみだったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Oh yes, he did love his entertainment programs, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm, conspiratorial agreement. A small knowing smile in the voice. She's meeting him halfway into his memory, gently correcting the detail without making it feel like correction.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがある映画のラストシーンに涙された
lines.en: Gran, I remember your father tearing up during the ending of a film once.
lines.style: Tender, searching — not quite certain of the exact moment but sure of the feeling. Slow pacing. Slight wonder in his voice, as if seeing his father-in-law anew through that memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、最近ポッドキャスティングを聴かれてたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: You know, he was listening to podcasts just recently, weren't you, dear?
lines.style: Light correction wrapped in affection. Gently steering him back to the present. Playful lilt — she's keeping him here with her, not letting him drift too far into the past.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがヤンキースの中継を観られた
lines.en: Gran, he used to watch the Yankees games back then.
lines.style: Quiet certainty settling over the words. Each memory is solid, held carefully. A small sad smile underneath — not quite reaching the surface, but there.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、地域のソフトボール大会に出られたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and you played in the local softball tournament yourself, didn't you, love?
lines.style: Warm, knowing redirection. A little firmness — she's bringing him back to his own life, to what he did. Not unkindly. The word 'love' lands softly at the end.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがホステス物の文学を分析された
lines.en: Gran, your father — he used to analyze those literary novels about hostesses.
lines.style: Voice trails into wonderment. The memory is softer, more fragile than the others. Searching for why he's telling her this. Long pause before speaking, hesitant quality.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お友達とタッグを組んで仕事をされたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: You worked with your friend on jobs together, didn't you? Both of you.
lines.style: Patient, warm close. A gentle anchor back to his present self, his own value. Tender finality — this memory is hers to hold, and she's offering it back to him.
